title: Pre-History, Indus Valley, Vedic Period & Mahajanapadas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bhimbetka:
1. The rock shelters are located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh.
2. The site is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
3. Its paintings belong exclusively to the Neolithic period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Bhimbetka (Raisen, MP) was inscribed in 2003 and has paintings from the Upper Palaeolithic and Mesolithic onwards into historical times, with the Mesolithic hunting and dancing scenes most prominent. 'Exclusively Neolithic' is wrong because the sequence is far longer.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture (Prehistoric rock art); Spectrum Ancient

questions.q: Which one of the following sites in the Bolan region of Balochistan gives the earliest evidence of farming and herding in the Indian subcontinent (c. 7000 BCE)?
questions.e: Mehrgarh shows wheat and barley cultivation and herding of cattle, sheep and goat, a long settled background from which the Indus cities later grew. Burzahom, Koldihwa and Chirand are Neolithic sites too, but of Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar respectively and later.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of Harappan sites and the rivers on which they are located:
1. Lothal : Bhogava
2. Ropar : Beas
3. Kalibangan : Yamuna
4. Harappa : Indus
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only Lothal (Bhogava, Gujarat) is correct. Ropar is on the Sutlej, Kalibangan on the (dried) Ghaggar-Hakra in Rajasthan, and Harappa on the (old course of the) Ravi.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1; Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q: Which one of the following Harappan sites is noted for the absence of a citadel and for evidence of bead making?
questions.e: Chanhudaro, on the Indus in Sindh, is the standard example of a Harappan settlement without a citadel, and was a craft centre for beads. Kalibangan, Dholavira and Banawali all had fortified or separately walled citadel sections.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Bipan/R.S. Sharma Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Dholavira:
1. It lies on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
2. Unlike most Harappan cities, its settlement was divided into three parts.
3. It was first excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in the 1950s.
4. It has remains of reservoirs and channels for conserving water.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are right. Dholavira's water management in a dry region is its hallmark; the large-scale excavation was by R.S. Bisht of the ASI from 1990, not Wheeler.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1; UNESCO WHC listing 2021

questions.q: Which one of the following Harappan sites is associated with an artificial dockyard excavated by S.R. Rao?
questions.e: Lothal on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat had a tidal dock, fitting its role as a port and bead-making centre. The others lie inland or have no dock identified.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Mohenjodaro was laid out in two parts, a smaller elevated citadel to the west and a larger lower town to the east.
Statement-II: The Great Bath and the granary were located in the lower town.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct, but the Great Bath and the granary stood on the citadel mound; the lower town held residential quarters and craft areas.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan weights and measures:
1. Weights were commonly made of bronze.
2. The lower weights followed a binary series (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and so on).
3. Weights were broadly standardised across Harappan sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Weights were usually cubical and made of chert, not bronze. They followed the binary series in the lower range and were uniform over the whole region, which supports centralised control over trade.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 1; Spectrum

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Harappan seals and script is NOT correct?
o: Steatite was the commonest material for seals.
Most seals carry long inscriptions of several hundred signs each.
Seals were probably used to mark or authenticate goods.
questions.e: Most Harappan inscriptions are very short, with only a handful of signs, which is one reason decipherment has failed; no long text or bilingual has been found.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following metals/materials was NOT known to the Harappans?
questions.e: The Harappan culture was Chalcolithic/Bronze Age; copper, bronze, gold and silver were in use, but iron came to the subcontinent about a thousand years after the mature Harappan phase.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan agriculture:
1. Cotton was cultivated and used for cloth.
2. Husks of rice have been found at Lothal and Rangpur.
3. Iron ploughshares were used for tilling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Cotton and rice are both attested, with rice husks at Lothal and Rangpur. Iron was unknown, so ploughs (terracotta models and the Kalibangan furrows) were not iron-shod.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan:
1. The ploughed field found there belongs to the Mature Harappan phase.
2. It has fire altars, indicating ritual practice.
3. Its name means 'black bangles'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The furrowed field belongs to the pre-Harappan (Early Harappan) level, not the Mature phase. Fire altars were found in houses and on the citadel, and the name Kalibangan means black bangles.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order (earliest first) of these cultural stages?
o: Mesolithic microliths - Palaeolithic hand axes - Neolithic polished celts - Chalcolithic painted pottery
Palaeolithic hand axes - Neolithic polished celts - Mesolithic microliths - Chalcolithic painted pottery
Palaeolithic hand axes - Mesolithic microliths - Chalcolithic painted pottery - Neolithic polished celts
Palaeolithic hand axes - Mesolithic microliths - Neolithic polished celts - Chalcolithic painted pottery
questions.e: Stone tool technology moved from large chipped tools (Palaeolithic) to tiny microliths (Mesolithic), then polished celts with farming (Neolithic), and finally the first use of copper (Chalcolithic).
questions.s: NCERT Class 6 Ch 2; Spectrum
questions.h: Old, Middle, New stone, then copper

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mesolithic age in India:
1. Microliths were typical of the stone tool industry.
2. Adamgarh and Bagor yielded the earliest evidence of domestication of animals in India.
3. People depended mainly on settled agriculture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Microliths and early animal herding at Adamgarh (MP) and Bagor (Rajasthan) mark the period. Subsistence was still hunting, fishing and gathering; settled agriculture is the mark of the Neolithic.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Nitin Singhania

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its Neolithic feature?
o: Burzahom (Kashmir) : pit dwellings and burial of pet dogs with owners
Chirand (Bihar) : extensive use of iron tools
Koldihwa (Uttar Pradesh) : early evidence of rice cultivation
Piklihal (Karnataka) : ash mounds linked with cattle herding
questions.e: Chirand is noted for its bone tools and a large number of bone implements, not iron. The other three pairs are standard Neolithic features.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Jorwe culture, with major excavated sites such as Inamgaon on the Ghod river, belongs to which phase in western Maharashtra?
questions.e: Jorwe-Inamgaon was a copper-stone farming culture, with houses, granaries, and burials of children under house floors. It is not a hunter-gatherer or iron-age culture.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Coins have not been found in the mature Harappan cities.
Statement-II: Exchange in Harappan towns was probably carried out through barter, assisted by seals and standard weights.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: With no coinage, goods were swapped and the seals and uniform weights helped regulate and authenticate exchanges, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Harappa was excavated by R.D. Banerji.
2. Mohenjodaro was excavated by R.D. Banerji.
3. Large-scale excavation at Dholavira was led by R.S. Bisht.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Harappa was first excavated by Daya Ram Sahni (1921) and Mohenjodaro by R.D. Banerji (1922). Dholavira, found by J.P. Joshi, was excavated by R.S. Bisht of the ASI from 1990. Statement 1 swaps the names.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 1
questions.h: Sahni at Harappa, Banerji at Mohenjodaro

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT true of Harappan religion?
o: Monumental temples housing idols were the centre of every city.
Terracotta female figurines are often interpreted as mother goddess images.
A seated figure on a seal is often called 'proto-Shiva'.
Trees such as the pipal are depicted on seals.
questions.e: No temple has been conclusively identified at a Harappan site; evidence of belief comes from figurines, seals and fire altars.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q: The Mature (Urban) Harappan phase is dated by NCERT to about:
questions.e: The mature phase fits between c. 2600 and 1900 BCE; later phases saw regional cultures replace the great cities, and 1500-1000 BCE is in the Vedic horizon.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sources of Harappan raw materials:
1. Copper was obtained from Khetri in Rajasthan.
2. Lapis lazuli came mainly from Gujarat.
3. Shortughai in northern Afghanistan was a Harappan trading outpost.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Khetri copper and the Shortughai outpost (near the lapis sources of Badakhshan) are right. Lapis lazuli was imported from Afghanistan, not mined in Gujarat.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 1

questions.q: Which animal motif appears most frequently on Harappan seals?
questions.e: The unicorn is by far the commonest seal motif. The horse is not shown on seals, an important contrast with the Vedic cattle-and-horse society.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q: Who discovered, in 1863 at Pallavaram near Madras, the first Palaeolithic stone tool found in India?
questions.e: Robert Bruce Foote of the Geological Survey picked up a hand axe at Pallavaram, starting the study of Indian prehistory. Cunningham, Marshall and Wheeler are linked to historical archaeology and the Indus sites.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Nitin Singhania Ch on Prehistoric India

questions.q: A pottery of red clay with black painted designs, made on the wheel, is most characteristic of which culture?
questions.e: Harappan pots were wheel-made, red slipped and painted in black. Painted Grey Ware belongs to the later Vedic phase, NBPW to the Mahajanapada-Mauryan phase.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1
questions.h: Harappa red, PGW grey, NBPW black

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan overseas contacts:
1. Mesopotamian texts refer to the Indus region as Meluhha.
2. Dilmun is identified with Bahrain.
3. Magan refers to China.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Meluhha was the Mesopotamian name for the Indus land and Dilmun is generally identified with Bahrain. Magan is placed in the Oman region, not China.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rigveda:
1. The Gayatri Mantra, attributed to Vishwamitra, occurs in Mandala 3.
2. The Purusha Sukta occurs in Mandala 10.
3. Mandala 9 is devoted to Indra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mandala 3 (Vishwamitra) carries the Gayatri mantra and the late Mandala 10 holds the Purusha Sukta on the origin of varnas. Mandala 9 is the Soma mandala, not Indra's.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Which one of the following gives the correct order of Vedic literature from earliest to latest?
questions.e: Hymns came first, then ritual commentaries (Brahmanas), forest texts (Aranyakas) and finally philosophical Upanishads.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Ancient India / R.S. Sharma

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Rigvedic king was not an absolute ruler.
Statement-II: Tribal assemblies such as the Sabha and the Samiti limited his authority.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Sabha and Samiti, with the Vidatha, discussed tribal affairs and the choice of the chief. Their influence checked royal power, which grew only in the later Vedic period.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna):
1. It was fought on the banks of the Yamuna.
2. Sudas of the Bharata tribe led one side.
3. Vasishtha was the priest of Sudas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The battle was fought on the Parushni (Ravi), not the Yamuna. Sudas of the Bharatas defeated a confederacy of ten tribes that included the Purus; the Bharatas later merged with the Purus to form the Kurus.
questions.s: R.S. Sharma; Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of Rigvedic names of rivers and their modern names:
1. Vitasta : Jhelum
2. Askini : Chenab
3. Parushni : Ravi
4. Shutudri : Sutlej
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are right. Vipasa is the Beas, Kubha the Kabul and Gomati the Gomal, which is where students usually trip.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the later Vedic period (c. 1000-600 BCE)?
o: Centre of culture shifted to the upper Ganga-Yamuna doab
Kuru and Panchala became prominent tribal kingdoms
Sabha and Samiti gained greater power over the king
questions.e: As kings grew stronger through large sacrifices, the Sabha and Samiti declined in importance. The other three developments are all later Vedic features.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Which Rigvedic term, literally meaning 'search for cows', came to denote war or fighting?
questions.e: Cattle were the chief form of wealth, so wars were gavishti. Godhuli is a time of day, duhitri (daughter) meant 'one who milks cows', and gotra meant a cow-pen.
questions.s: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past; Old NCERT Ancient India
questions.h: Cow-wealth society: war = search for cows

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Purusha Sukta:
1. Brahmanas arose from the mouth of the primeval being.
2. Vaishyas arose from the arms.
3. Shudras arose from the feet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The hymn says Brahmanas came from the mouth, Rajanya (Kshatriyas) from the arms, Vaishyas from the thighs and Shudras from the feet. It appears in the late Mandala 10 and gave religious sanction to the varna order.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 6 Ch 6

questions.q: In later Vedic ritual, which sacrifice included a chariot race in which the king's chariot was made to win?
questions.e: The Vajapeya, a royal rite, centred on a chariot race. The Rajasuya was the consecration, and the Ashvamedha was the horse sacrifice for unchallenged sway over territory.
questions.s: R.S. Sharma; Spectrum Ancient India
questions.h: Rajasuya crown, Vajapeya race, Ashvamedha horse

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the later Vedic period, marriage within the same gotra was prohibited.
Statement-II: Gotra, literally a cow-pen, came to denote descent from a common ancestor.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Members of one gotra were regarded as descendants of a common ancestor, so marrying inside it was treated like marrying within the family. Gotra exogamy emerged in this period.
questions.s: R.S. Sharma; Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gargi Vachaknavi took part in a philosophical debate at the court of Janaka of Videha.
2. Maitreyi was the sister of Gargi.
3. Ghosha, Apala and Lopamudra are associated with Rigvedic hymns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya is in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, and Ghosha, Apala and Lopamudra are women associated with Rigvedic hymns. Maitreyi was Yajnavalkya's wife, not Gargi's sister.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 11 Ancient India

questions.q: Which one of the following Upanishad-teaching pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Satyameva Jayate, India's national motto, comes from the Mundaka Upanishad. The Katha Upanishad is known for the Nachiketa-Yama dialogue.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania; Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q: Which one of the following priests is correctly paired with the Veda he is associated with?
questions.e: The Hotri recited the Rigveda, the Udgatri sang the Samaveda, the Adhvaryu performed the rites with Yajurveda formulae and the Brahma oversaw the ritual with the Atharvaveda.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Vedanga?
questions.e: The six Vedangas are Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda and Jyotisha. Nyaya is one of the six schools of philosophy.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania; Spectrum Ancient India
questions.h: Shiksha Kalpa Vyakarana Nirukta Chhanda Jyotisha

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rigvedic deities:
1. Indra, the fort-destroyer, has the largest number of hymns.
2. Varuna was regarded as the upholder of Rita, the cosmic order.
3. Pushan was the god of thunder and war.
4. Agni acted as the intermediary between gods and men.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Pushan is a pastoral deity guarding roads and herds; Indra is the thunder and war god.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 11 Ancient India

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of Mahajanapada and capital is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Vajji's centre was Vaishali; Rajagriha was the early capital of Magadha. The other three pairs are right.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q: Which of the 16 Mahajanapadas was located in the south, on the banks of the Godavari?
questions.e: Assaka was the southernmost Mahajanapada. Avanti lay in the Malwa region, Chedi in Bundelkhand and Vatsa around Kaushambi.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; R.S. Sharma

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Vajji sangha was governed by an assembly of clan chiefs, not a hereditary king.
Statement-II: The Lichchhavis of Vaishali were the most prominent clan of the Vajji confederacy.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true, but the second only names the leading clan; it does not explain why the polity lacked a monarch. The Malla republics were of the same type.
questions.s: R.S. Sharma; Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Magadha emerged as the most powerful Mahajanapada.
Statement-II: Magadha had fertile Gangetic plains, nearby iron ores and forests with elephants.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Surplus from rice lands, iron for weapons and tools, and elephants for the army gave Magadha a decisive advantage; rivers and the hill-ringed Rajagriha added security and communication.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2

questions.q: Which one is the correct chronological order of the dynasties of Magadha?
questions.e: Bimbisara's Haryankas were followed by the Shishunagas (who destroyed Avanti), then the Nandas, who were replaced by Chandragupta Maurya.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about early Magadha:
1. Bimbisara ruled from Rajagriha.
2. Ajatashatru overcame the Vajji confederacy.
3. Udayin shifted the capital to Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Rajagriha (Girivraja) was Bimbisara's capital, Ajatashatru crushed the Vajjis, and Udayin moved the capital to Pataliputra, better placed on the Ganga for control of trade.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Upinder Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nandas:
1. They ruled from Rajagriha.
2. Mahapadma Nanda is described in the Puranas as the destroyer of all Kshatriyas.
3. Dhananda was ruling Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Nandas ruled from Pataliputra. The Puranas present Mahapadma as destroyer of the old Kshatriya dynasties, and Dhananda (Greek Agrammes/Xandrames) was the last Nanda, overthrown by Chandragupta.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Persian contact with north-west India:
1. Darius I's inscriptions mention Gandhara and Hindush among his provinces.
2. Kharosthi script is written from left to right.
3. Kharosthi was derived from the Aramaic script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Darius I's inscriptions list Gandhara and Hindush. Kharosthi, written from right to left, grew out of Aramaic used by Persian administration.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Upinder Singh

questions.q: Alexander's army refused to march farther east and turned back at which river?
questions.e: After defeating Porus on the Jhelum (326 BCE), Alexander's war-weary soldiers refused to cross the Beas, ending his advance toward the Nanda empire.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; Upinder Singh

questions.q: Which one of the following is the earliest type of coin issued in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.e: Punch-marked coins (karshapana) of silver, used by the Mahajanapadas, mark the first coinage. The other coin series came after the Mauryan period.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient India; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2
